experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes
experiences.description: Enjoy world-class skiing across the interconnected slopes of Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. The Jungfrau Ski Region offers over 200km of groomed pistes suitable for all skill levels, making it perfect for families with mixed skiing abilities. Rent equipment on-site and take advantage of ski school lessons for younger children.

experiences.name: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride
experiences.description: Board the legendary Glacier Express from Zermatt to St. Moritz for a breathtaking 8-hour panoramic journey through snow-covered Alpine valleys, frozen rivers, and dramatic mountain passes. Family-friendly with panoramic windows and dining car service offering Swiss specialties. A magical winter experience requiring no physical exertion.
experiences.location: Zermatt to St. Moritz, Valais & Graubünden

experiences.name: Tobogganing on the Fläsch-Maienfeld Run
experiences.description: Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family toboggan runs, a 3.5km natural ice track descending through pine forests and Alpine meadows. Sleds are available for rent at the top station, and the run is suitable for children aged 5 and up. A fantastic alternative to skiing that the whole family will love.

experiences.name: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Class
experiences.description: Participate in a hands-on traditional Swiss fondue and raclette cooking class hosted by a local Alpine family in Gruyères. Learn the centuries-old art of cheese-making, taste regional varieties, and sit down to enjoy the meal you prepared together. An immersive cultural experience that combines food, history, and family bonding.

experiences.name: Snowshoeing and Winter Hiking in Saas-Fee
experiences.description: Explore the car-free Alpine village of Saas-Fee on guided snowshoe trails winding through pristine snow-covered forests and glacier viewpoints. Guides provide all equipment including snowshoes and poles, and routes are tailored to family fitness levels. End the excursion with hot chocolate at a traditional mountain hut for a cozy Alpine finish.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — late night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, settle into your room, and rest after your flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Swiss Alps airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Take an airport transfer or regional train to your accommodation. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, grab a light snack from the hotel vending machine or a nearby 24-hour convenience store, and get a good night's sleep to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — travel day
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Light snack from hotel minimarket or 24-hour convenience store near the resort (budget CHF 5–10). Pack some trail mix or granola bars from your carry-on luggage.

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival simple. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to save money — shared shuttle services are significantly cheaper than private taxis in Switzerland. Confirm check-in details with Aegean Bliss Resort for late-night arrival. Exchange some cash or ensure your card works internationally before leaving the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a hearty breakfast at the resort, then head out to explore the local village on foot. Take a leisurely walk through the alpine village center, browse local shops, and get oriented with the surroundings. Visit the tourist information office to pick up free maps, discount ski passes, and family activity brochures. Many Swiss villages offer free pedestrian zones with stunning mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a beginner-friendly ski slope nearby. Many Swiss Alps resorts offer half-day ski rentals that are more budget-friendly than full-day packages. Look for family ski schools that offer group lessons for children and adults — group lessons are significantly cheaper than private instruction. Spend 2–3 hours on the bunny slopes getting comfortable on skis.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to warm up. Take a short stroll through the illuminated village in the evening — Swiss alpine villages are beautifully lit in winter. Visit a local fondue restaurant for a classic Swiss experience. Many offer budget-friendly set menus especially for families.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort if included, or grab bread, cheese, and yogurt from a local Migros or Coop supermarket (budget CHF 8–12 per person).
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch on the slopes — pack sandwiches and hot chocolate in a thermos from the supermarket to avoid expensive mountain restaurant prices (budget CHF 5–8 per person).
meals.dinner: Local village fondue restaurant — look for set menus or 'tourist menus' which are typically CHF 20–30 per person. Children often eat free or at half price.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a multi-day ski pass if you plan to ski for 3+ days — it's considerably cheaper than single-day passes. Check if the resort or local ski area offers a family discount package. Rent ski equipment from a local rental shop in the village rather than at the ski resort itself to save 20–30%.

day_by_day.morning: Full day of skiing! Wake up early to hit the slopes before crowds arrive. Take the gondola or ski lift up to intermediate slopes if your family is comfortable. Many Swiss ski resorts open lifts around 8:30–9:00 AM. Early morning snow conditions are typically the best of the day. Take a group ski lesson if needed to improve technique.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing through the afternoon. Take a mid-afternoon break at a mountain hut (Bergrestaurant) for a warm drink. Try a traditional Swiss rösti or soup which are more affordable mountain meal options. Explore different runs and trails suited to various skill levels within your ski pass zone.
day_by_day.evening: After returning from the slopes, enjoy the resort's facilities — check if Aegean Bliss Resort has a sauna or hot tub, which are perfect for tired muscles. Have a relaxed family dinner at the resort restaurant or cook a simple meal if you have access to a kitchenette.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or supermarket-bought items like instant oatmeal, fruit, and yogurt to fuel up before skiing (budget CHF 8–10 per person).
meals.lunch: Mountain hut lunch — order soup, rösti, or a shared plate to keep costs down. Avoid full restaurant meals on the mountain (budget CHF 15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner using groceries from Migros or Coop — pasta with Swiss cheese sauce, bread, and salad is a filling and budget-friendly option (budget CHF 10–15 for the family).

day_by_day.notes: Wear moisture-wicking base layers and proper ski socks to stay comfortable all day. Apply sunscreen even in winter — UV rays reflect strongly off snow at altitude. Keep hydrated as mountain air is very dry. Children should always wear helmets, which can be rented alongside ski equipment.

day_by_day.morning: Take a rest day from skiing and explore winter hiking trails. Many Swiss alpine areas maintain groomed winter walking paths that are free to use. Bundle up and take a scenic snowshoe walk — snowshoe rentals are much cheaper than ski rentals (around CHF 10–15 per day). Enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of the Alps without the cost of lift tickets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Swiss museum or cultural center — many offer free or discounted family admission. Alternatively, explore the village's traditional Swiss architecture, visit a local church or chapel, and browse artisan shops for locally made Swiss products. Look for a toboggan run (Rodelbahn) — these are extremely popular with families and very affordable (CHF 5–10 per person including sled rental).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a family-friendly evening activity such as ice skating at an outdoor rink, which is common in Swiss alpine villages in winter. Many outdoor rinks offer free or very low-cost skating with minimal equipment rental fees. Warm up afterward with hot chocolate at a local café.

meals.breakfast: Supermarket-bought breakfast — Swiss muesli, milk, fruit, and bread with butter and jam (budget CHF 6–8 per person).
meals.lunch: Grab a takeaway bratwurst or pretzel from a street vendor or bakery in the village — a classic Swiss budget lunch (budget CHF 8–12 per person).
meals.dinner: Visit a local Beiz (traditional Swiss pub-restaurant) for a budget dinner. Order Älplermagronen (Swiss alpine macaroni) or Käseschnitten (cheese toast) — hearty, traditional, and affordable (budget CHF 18–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: A rest day from skiing is important for families with children to avoid fatigue and injury. Winter hiking and tobogganing are equally exciting for kids. Check local event boards in the village — free concerts, markets, or cultural events are often held on weekends. The Swiss Travel Pass or regional guest cards (often provided free by hotels) may offer discounts on local transport and activities.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the ski slopes for another full day of skiing. By now your family should be more confident on skis. Try exploring different sectors of the ski area and challenge yourselves with slightly more advanced runs. Many Swiss ski resorts have excellent trail maps — pick one up at the lift station and plan your route for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, try a different winter sport — look for cross-country skiing (Langlauf) trails in the valley. Cross-country skiing is much cheaper than downhill skiing (no lift pass required) and is a wonderful way to explore the alpine landscape. Equipment rental is affordable at CHF 15–20 per day.
day_by_day.evening: Treat the family to a special dinner tonight at a mid-range Swiss restaurant. Look for early bird specials or set menus. This is a great opportunity to try Swiss specialties like raclette — where cheese is melted tableside and scraped over potatoes and vegetables.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or homemade — boil eggs, serve with Swiss bread and cheese purchased from the supermarket (budget CHF 7–10 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of soup and sandwiches from the supermarket to eat at a mountain picnic area or rest hut — save significantly compared to mountain restaurants (budget CHF 5–8 per person).
meals.dinner: Raclette dinner at a local Swiss restaurant — look for set menus around CHF 25–35 per person. Many restaurants offer children's portions at reduced prices.

day_by_day.notes: If you've purchased a multi-day ski pass, check how many days remain and plan accordingly. Cross-country skiing is an excellent low-impact alternative for family members who may be tired of downhill skiing. Many Swiss villages have free cross-country loops maintained by the municipality. Check for any night skiing events — some resorts offer evening skiing on select days which can be a magical experience for families.

day_by_day.morning: Take a scenic train or cable car ride to a high-altitude viewpoint. Switzerland's mountain railway network is world-famous — even short scenic rides offer spectacular views. Check if your regional guest card offers free or discounted rides. Visit a high-altitude observation platform for panoramic Alpine views — a truly memorable experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Swiss farm or dairy if available in the area — many alpine farms welcome visitors in winter and offer free or low-cost tours where you can see how Swiss cheese and chocolate are made. Alternatively, spend the afternoon at a family-friendly indoor activity center or swimming pool — many Swiss resort towns have heated indoor pools open to the public for a small fee (CHF 8–15 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Host a self-catered fondue night in your hotel room or common area if facilities allow. Purchase a fondue set and ingredients from Migros or Coop — it's a fun, interactive, and very Swiss family activity at a fraction of restaurant prices. Alternatively, many supermarkets sell ready-made fondue kits.

meals.breakfast: Full supermarket breakfast spread — yogurt parfait with Swiss granola, fresh fruit, and Swiss hot chocolate (budget CHF 8–10 per person).
meals.lunch: Bakery lunch in the village — fresh bread rolls, quiche, and pastries from a local Bäckerei (bakery). Swiss bakeries offer excellent quality at reasonable prices (budget CHF 10–15 per person).
meals.dinner: DIY fondue night using a supermarket fondue kit — Gruyère and Emmental cheese fondue with bread cubes, potatoes, and vegetables. Budget CHF 10–15 for the whole family, making it the most economical and fun dinner of the trip.

day_by_day.notes: The Swiss rail network is efficient and scenic — even a 20-minute train ride through alpine scenery is worth the cost. Look for combination tickets that include transport and attraction entry. If you have a Swiss Travel Pass, many mountain railways are included or heavily discounted. Buy supermarket fondue kits the day before to ensure availability.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — take one last walk through the village to soak in the alpine atmosphere. Visit any shops you haven't explored yet and pick up budget-friendly Swiss souvenirs such as Swiss chocolate bars from the supermarket (much cheaper than souvenir shops), local postcards, or small Swiss army knife keychains. Take final photos of the stunning mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack your bags and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your departure time, you may have time for a final short activity such as a brief snowshoe walk, a visit to a local café for one last Swiss hot chocolate, or simply relaxing and reflecting on the week's adventures. Head to the transport hub for your onward journey.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from the Swiss Alps. If you have an evening flight or connection, spend time at the airport or train station. Swiss airports have good facilities including reasonably priced food options. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, winter sports, and family memories in one of the world's most beautiful mountain destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a supermarket grab-and-go — Swiss yogurt, a croissant, and fresh juice (budget CHF 8–10 per person).
meals.lunch: Quick and affordable lunch at a supermarket deli counter or takeaway bakery before departing — perfect for eating on the go (budget CHF 8–12 per person).
meals.dinner: Airport or train station meal — look for Migros or Coop restaurant outlets in Swiss transport hubs which offer quality food at much lower prices than airport restaurants (budget CHF 15–20 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the resort. Store luggage at the hotel reception if you need extra time before departing. Buy any last-minute Swiss chocolate or souvenirs at Migros or Coop supermarkets at the airport — prices are much more reasonable than duty-free luxury shops. Keep receipts for any VAT refund claims on purchases over CHF 300. Safe travels!

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Swiss Alps. Check-in, unpack, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Aegean Bliss Resort at approximately 23:30 after transfer. Light welcome snack or room service if available. Rest and prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: Meal on flight or grab a snack at the airport before departure.
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or airport dining.
meals.dinner: Late-night room service or a light snack from the resort's available options upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day only — no sightseeing or activities planned. Confirm transfer arrangements in advance. Pack layers for the cold Alpine night. Keep luggage accessible for a quick check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast to recover from travel. Afterward, head to the resort's ski rental shop or nearby ski hire center to rent equipment and purchase lift passes. Spend the late morning getting oriented on the beginner or intermediate slopes near the resort — ideal for shaking off jet lag and warming up your ski legs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the featured experience: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes. Head to Grindelwald or Wengen's interconnected ski area for an afternoon of world-class skiing. Take advantage of well-groomed runs across varying difficulty levels, perfect for families. Ski instructors are available on-site for beginners or younger children.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by 17:00. Relax in the resort spa or lounge area. Enjoy a classic Swiss dinner at the resort's restaurant or a nearby Alpine eatery in the village.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — eggs, cold cuts, cheeses, fresh bread, and hot drinks.
meals.lunch: Mountain-top restaurant on the Jungfrau slopes — try a hearty rösti (Swiss potato pancake) or a bowl of goulash soup with bread.
meals.dinner: Cozy Alpine restaurant near the resort — order raclette or a cheese fondue for a classic Swiss experience. Budget approx. CHF 35–50 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Book ski rentals and lift passes online in advance to save time and money. Dress in thermal layers, waterproof ski jacket, and gloves. Apply high-SPF sunscreen — Alpine UV levels are intense even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a guided Snowshoeing and Winter Hiking experience in Saas-Fee. Depart early from the resort and travel to the car-free Alpine village of Saas-Fee. A certified guide will lead your family through pristine snow-covered forests and open meadows on snowshoes, with stunning views of the surrounding glaciers. Suitable for all ages and fitness levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the snowshoe tour, explore Saas-Fee village on foot. Browse local artisan shops, visit the Alpine Museum, or enjoy a horse-drawn sleigh ride through the village center — a delightful family activity. Return to the resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Wind down with a family movie night or board games in the resort lounge. Alternatively, visit the resort's heated indoor pool or hot tub to soothe tired muscles.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go breakfast from the resort — yogurt, granola, fresh fruit, and coffee/hot chocolate before the early departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Saas-Fee at a local mountain café — try Älplermagronen (Alpine mac and cheese with apple sauce) or a hearty soup and sandwich combo. Budget approx. CHF 20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby pizzeria — wood-fired pizza and pasta are popular and budget-friendly options in Swiss Alpine villages. Budget approx. CHF 25–40 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe tours in Saas-Fee can be booked through the resort concierge or the Saas-Fee tourist office. Saas-Fee is car-free — a shuttle or electric taxi will take you from the parking area into the village. Bring a backpack with water, snacks, and a camera.

day_by_day.morning: Full day dedicated to the Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride. Board the legendary Glacier Express from Zermatt to St. Moritz (or a partial segment if a full-day journey is too long for younger children). Depart early morning and settle into panoramic carriages as the train winds through 91 tunnels and over 291 bridges, passing through some of Switzerland's most dramatic Alpine scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Glacier Express journey through the afternoon, passing through the Rhine Gorge (the 'Swiss Grand Canyon'), the Oberalp Pass, and the Engadin Valley. Enjoy the onboard dining car for a relaxed mid-journey lunch with views. Arrive at St. Moritz or your designated stop in the early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort via train or organized transfer. Enjoy a quiet dinner at the resort to rest after the long but scenic travel day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — full buffet to fuel up for the journey.
meals.lunch: Onboard dining car on the Glacier Express — a set three-course menu is available (approx. CHF 40–55 per adult). Pre-book your meal reservation when purchasing train tickets.
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort restaurant — a warm soup, salad, and grilled fish or chicken. Budget approx. CHF 30–45 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Book Glacier Express tickets well in advance — they sell out quickly, especially in peak winter season. A panoramic seat reservation is mandatory (approx. CHF 13–33 extra). Consider a partial route (e.g., Zermatt to Andermatt) if traveling with young children to reduce journey time. Bring snacks, entertainment for kids, and a camera with a fully charged battery.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery and leisure morning at the resort after the long train day. Sleep in, enjoy a relaxed breakfast, and spend time at the resort's amenities — indoor pool, spa, or a gentle walk around the resort grounds in the snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head out for the Tobogganing on the Fläsch-Maienfeld Run — one of Switzerland's most thrilling family toboggan runs. The 3.5km natural ice track is a highlight for families and provides an adrenaline-filled afternoon. Sleds can be rented on-site. Multiple runs are possible within a 2–3 hour session. Suitable for children and adults alike.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by 17:30. Freshen up and head out for a fun family dinner in the village. Consider a fondue restaurant for a social, interactive dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Full resort buffet breakfast — take your time and enjoy a slow morning.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks from a local bakery near the toboggan run — grab fresh pretzels, sandwiches, and hot chocolate from a nearby kiosk. Budget approx. CHF 10–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Traditional Swiss fondue restaurant in the local village — cheese fondue for the table, served with bread cubes, pickles, and pearl onions. Budget approx. CHF 35–50 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Wear waterproof outerwear and helmets for tobogganing — helmets are often available for rental. Children must be accompanied by an adult on the run. The Fläsch-Maienfeld run may require a short drive or train ride from the resort — confirm directions with the concierge. Arrive early in the afternoon to maximize run time before dusk.

day_by_day.morning: Participate in the Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Class hosted by a local Alpine chef. This hands-on culinary experience teaches families how to prepare traditional raclette and fondue from scratch, including the history and culture behind Switzerland's most iconic dishes. Great for kids and adults — interactive, educational, and delicious.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Jungfrau Region Slopes for a final full afternoon of skiing. With a few days of practice under your belt, push yourself to try more challenging runs or explore new areas of the interconnected ski network. Families can enjoy ski races, fun parks, or guided group lessons if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner at one of the resort's signature restaurants or a highly-rated local Alpine restaurant. Toast to a wonderful trip with a glass of Swiss wine or a warm Glühwein (mulled wine).

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — fuel up before the cooking class.
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the fondue and cheese-making class — lunch is typically included as part of the class experience.
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual Alpine restaurant — try a three-course meal featuring local specialties such as venison stew, Alpine trout, or Berner Platte (a hearty meat and sauerkraut platter). Budget approx. CHF 50–70 per adult for a special farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Class in advance through the resort concierge or a local culinary school — class sizes are often limited. Saturday slopes can be busier with weekend visitors — arrive at the ski lifts early in the afternoon to avoid peak queues. Keep lift passes from Day 2 if they are multi-day passes.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Enjoy a relaxed last breakfast at the resort. Take a short scenic walk or snowshoe stroll around the resort grounds to soak in the Alpine views one last time. Pack and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, visit a local souvenir shop or artisan market in the nearby village to pick up Swiss chocolates, cheese, fondue sets, or carved wooden gifts for family and friends back home. Head to the airport with plenty of time for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Switzerland. Reflect on a wonderful week of skiing, scenic train journeys, tobogganing, and family memories in the breathtaking Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Final full resort buffet breakfast — enjoy all your favorites one last time.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick bite in the village before departure — try a Swiss bratwurst from a street stand or a fresh sandwich from a bakery. Budget approx. CHF 15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 — confirm with the resort. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport transfer, check-in, and security. Swiss duty-free shops at the airport offer excellent deals on Swiss chocolate (Lindt, Toblerone) and watches — a great last-minute gift option. Keep a small amount of Swiss Francs for tips or last-minute purchases.

meals.lunch: Not applicable — travel day

Pause mid-afternoon at a mountain-top sun terrace restaurant for hot chocolate and Alpine snacks with panoramic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a spa recovery session — heated indoor pool, sauna, and a 60-minute couple's or family relaxation massage. Freshen up before a gourmet dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort's lavish buffet breakfast — freshly baked croissants, smoked salmon, Swiss cheeses, seasonal fruits, eggs cooked to order, and freshly squeezed juices.
meals.lunch: Bergrestaurant Grindelwald First — panoramic mountain-top dining with fondue, rösti, and Alpine charcuterie platters. Premium Swiss wines available.
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort Signature Restaurant — 5-course tasting menu featuring pan-seared foie gras, truffle risotto, and slow-braised Swiss veal. Paired wine selection by the sommelier.

day_by_day.notes: Book ski school and private instructor at least 24 hours in advance through the concierge. Altitude sickness prevention: stay hydrated, avoid alcohol the first evening, and ascend gradually. Dress in breathable, waterproof ski layers.

day_by_day.morning: Tobogganing on the Fläsch-Maienfeld Run — Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family toboggan runs, a 3.5km natural ice track descending through pristine Alpine scenery. A private shuttle transfers the family to the run. Multiple descents available — a guaranteed highlight for children and adults alike. Safety briefing and premium sled rental included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Class — Participate in a hands-on traditional Swiss fondue and raclette cooking class hosted by a local Alpine cheesemaker. Learn the art of crafting authentic Gruyère and Appenzeller fondue, paired with crusty bread, pickles, and charcuterie. Each family member gets an apron and a recipe booklet as a keepsake.
day_by_day.evening: Snowshoeing twilight experience — A short guided snowshoe walk through illuminated forest trails near the resort at dusk, followed by a fireside aperitif of mulled wine and Swiss pastries. Return to the resort for a private in-suite dinner under the stars on your heated balcony.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — freshly made waffles with berry compote, smoked trout, avocado toast on sourdough, and specialty Swiss coffee blends.
meals.lunch: Post-fondue class meal — enjoy the fruits of your culinary labour with the full fondue spread prepared during the class, complemented by Swiss white wine (Fendant).
meals.dinner: Private in-suite dining experience — Châteaubriand for two (or family platter), roasted root vegetables, truffle butter, and a decadent Swiss chocolate lava cake for dessert. Curated wine pairing included.

day_by_day.notes: The Fläsch-Maienfeld toboggan run is approximately 45–60 minutes by private transfer from the Swiss Alps region. Confirm departure time with the concierge the evening prior. The fondue class typically lasts 2–3 hours and is fully family-friendly. Wear comfortable, waterproof boots for snowshoeing.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride — Board the legendary Glacier Express from Zermatt to St. Moritz for a breathtaking 8-hour panoramic journey through 91 tunnels and over 291 bridges. First-class Excellence Class carriage reserved for the family, featuring panoramic glass roofs, gourmet on-board dining, and personal attendant service. Depart early morning with private transfer to Zermatt station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Glacier Express continues — Pass through the dramatic Oberalp Pass (2,033m), the Rhine Gorge (the 'Swiss Grand Canyon'), and the Landwasser Viaduct. Enjoy the ever-changing Alpine landscape from the comfort of your luxury carriage with curated commentary from your private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in St. Moritz by late afternoon. Explore the glamorous village on foot — browse luxury boutiques (Cartier, Hermès, Prada) and enjoy the vibrant après-ski atmosphere. Private transfer back to the resort or an overnight stay in St. Moritz at Badrutt's Palace Hotel (optional upgrade). Gourmet dinner in St. Moritz.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh pastries, yogurt parfait, and espresso to go.
meals.lunch: On-board Glacier Express Excellence Class gourmet lunch — three-course meal featuring smoked salmon tartare, braised beef cheeks with Alpine vegetables, and a selection of Swiss desserts. Fine wine and Champagne pairings available.
meals.dinner: Chesa Veglia, St. Moritz — one of Switzerland's most celebrated Alpine restaurants, housed in a 17th-century Engadine farmhouse. Signature wood-fired pizza, grilled meats, and an exceptional wine cellar. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: The Glacier Express Excellence Class must be booked well in advance — confirm with the concierge immediately upon arrival. Private transfers to Zermatt and from St. Moritz are included in the luxury package. This is a full-day excursion; pack snacks, entertainment for children, and warm layers as temperatures drop through mountain passes.

day_by_day.morning: Snowshoeing and Winter Hiking in Saas-Fee — Explore the car-free Alpine village of Saas-Fee on guided snowshoe trails winding through pristine snow-covered forests and glacier viewpoints. A certified private mountain guide leads the family at a comfortable pace with frequent stops for photography. Saas-Fee is known as the 'Pearl of the Alps' — the views of the Fee Glacier and surrounding 4,000m peaks are extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by midday for a premium spa afternoon — access to the resort's full wellness facilities including an outdoor heated infinity pool overlooking the Alps, steam rooms, and a private family hydrotherapy session. Optional: book individual 90-minute deep-tissue or hot stone massages for adults.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private igloo dining experience — the resort arranges a romantic and adventurous dinner inside a custom-built snow igloo on the resort grounds, heated and decorated with candles and fur throws. A private chef serves a five-course Alpine tasting menu under a sky full of stars.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet — eggs benedict, freshly baked pastries, seasonal fruit platters, smoothie station, and Swiss muesli with warm milk.
meals.lunch: Mountain Hut Lunch in Saas-Fee — Walliserkanne Restaurant. Traditional Valais cuisine: raclette, air-dried beef (Bündnerfleisch), and hearty Alpine soup. Local Valais wines.
meals.dinner: Private igloo dining — 5-course tasting menu: amuse-bouche, seared scallops with cauliflower purée, venison carpaccio, slow-roasted rack of lamb with rosemary jus, and a white chocolate and raspberry mousse. Champagne and curated wine flight included.

day_by_day.notes: Saas-Fee is approximately 30–45 minutes by private transfer. The village is entirely car-free, so electric taxis and horse-drawn sleighs are used within the village — a wonderful experience for children. Book the igloo dining experience at least 48 hours in advance as it is highly sought after. Warm thermal underlayers are recommended for the igloo dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Advanced skiing day on the Jungfrau Region Slopes — return to the world-class Jungfrau ski area for a full day of skiing with your private instructor. Today focuses on more challenging red and black runs for confident skiers, while younger family members enjoy a dedicated ski school session with certified children's instructors. Take the Jungfraujoch cogwheel train to the 'Top of Europe' at 3,454m for unrivalled panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Heli-skiing experience (weather permitting) — a premium helicopter is arranged to transport the family to untouched off-piste powder fields accessible only by air. Guided by a certified mountain guide, this once-in-a-lifetime experience offers pristine untracked snow far from the crowds. Approximately 2–3 runs included.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski celebration at the resort's luxury lounge bar — live jazz, craft cocktails (Alpine herb gin & tonics, Champagne), and a curated charcuterie and cheese board. Transition into a private dining room for a celebratory farewell-eve dinner with the family.

meals.breakfast: Resort à la carte breakfast — eggs cooked to order, smoked salmon on blinis, freshly pressed orange juice, and artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Bergrestaurant Männlichen — mountaintop restaurant with sweeping views. Grilled Alpine trout, rösti with bacon and eggs, and warm apple strudel with vanilla sauce.
meals.dinner: Private dining room at Aegean Bliss Resort — 7-course chef's table experience with the Executive Chef. Seasonal Alpine ingredients, truffles, and a bespoke wine pairing journey through Swiss, French, and Italian vintages. Personalized menu cards as a keepsake.

day_by_day.notes: Heli-skiing is subject to weather and wind conditions — have a backup plan of additional piste skiing or a snowmobile tour. Confirm heli-skiing 24 hours in advance. The Jungfraujoch excursion requires warm clothing as temperatures can reach -15°C or below at the summit. Children must meet minimum age/weight requirements for heli-skiing — consult the guide.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — sleep in and enjoy a relaxed breakfast at the resort. Pack and prepare luggage with the assistance of your personal butler. Take a final gentle walk or snowshoe stroll through the resort grounds to soak in the last Alpine vistas. Visit the resort's boutique for Swiss souvenirs — premium chocolates (Läderach, Sprüngli), Swiss watches, and Alpine-themed gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell spa treatment — final 45-minute relaxation massage or facial at the resort spa. Check-out formalities handled seamlessly by the concierge team. Private luxury transfer arranged to the airport for your departure flight. En route, optional stop at a local artisan chocolate shop or Swiss delicatessen for last-minute premium gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — airport transfer and check-in. If the flight is late evening, relax in the airport's premium lounge with complimentary access arranged by the concierge.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — a lavish spread of everything enjoyed throughout the week: fresh pastries, eggs, smoked fish, Swiss cheeses, seasonal fruits, and a farewell Champagne toast.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort's terrace bistro — club sandwich with Alpine chicken, truffle fries, and a glass of Swiss Chasselas white wine.
meals.dinner: Airport premium lounge dining or on-board business/first-class meal (depending on flight schedule). The concierge can arrange a gourmet picnic hamper for the journey — filled with Swiss cheeses, charcuterie, chocolates, and a bottle of fine Swiss wine.

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all luggage is packed and ready the evening prior to avoid morning stress. The concierge will arrange ski equipment return and any outstanding billing. Request a detailed invoice and trip summary from the resort for records. Collect all ski passes, lift tickets, and activity vouchers as mementos. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for private transfer and airport check-in.

query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February 2026
